title: Back to New York with Pete Johnson; Louella visits
summary: The two went east for a job; Louella visited for a month and then called him home.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: So we took off, went to New York City. My wife, she didn't go. So I would call her up every day, see how she's doin'. So she said she gonna take off, come to New York and hang out with us awhile.
Pete sayin' "No, no, no, no, no, no," 'cause he left his wife in Chicago, too. He say, "No, no, no. That'd mess up our whole deal."
I say, "Well, I just got a brand new...you been married to your wife four...five years. I got this a brand new wife with me. I think it would be nice to have her come."
So I say, "I ain't gonna mess up. You ain't gonna be mad at all."
Say, "You get on one of them benders, stay out two...three days...you gonna get put out. Quick."
I say, "Well, I gotta take my chances." I say, "Maybe I'll do that. Maybe I won't. So I'll just go along till I see what I'm gonna do. Whatever happens gonna happen."

So she came to New York...stayed a month with us. We lived it up. We had a ball. We did everything you could do in New York City. I went back to John Hammonds. He got us some jobs. Made some more recordings. We livin' it up. So, finally, my wife went back to see about the house, an' she called me up one day and tol' me she was lone-some...for me to come home.
She said, "...back so we didn't need the money that bad no way. Come on home. You can get a job here in Chicago where I can see you every night."
